title: Sell Mineral Rights in Dunlevy, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Dunlevy, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: Dunlevy sits on the Monongahela in Washington County's Marcellus wet-gas footprint. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly from owners, cash offer.
heroLead: Dunlevy is a small river borough across from Speers, part of a chain of Monongahela River towns in Washington County where coal history and modern gas leasing sit layered on top of each other.
intro: The Monongahela River towns in this part of Washington County share a similar story: dense residential development built for coal and steel workers, surrounded by farmland that carried separate mineral history entirely. A Dunlevy family's mineral situation can depend a lot on whether their property is a small in-town lot or a larger parcel further from the river, since the deed history for each tends to look very different.
We check the specific recorded deed for your Dunlevy-area property before offering anything, since assuming based on a neighbor's situation can lead you astray here.

sections.heading: River Borough Density, Rural Mineral History Nearby
paragraphs: Dunlevy itself is compact, built up along the river, while the surrounding township holds more open farmland that's part of Washington County's broader wet-gas leasing footprint. If your family's interest is tied to a larger tract outside the dense borough core, it's more likely to be part of an active or potential drilling unit than a small in-town residential lot would be.
That said, in-town parcels aren't automatically excluded from mineral value, it depends on the deed and, in some cases, whether the operator's unit boundary happens to extend into the borough itself.

sections.heading: Coal-Era Deeds Along the River
paragraphs: Coal mining shaped this stretch of the Mon River valley long before any Marcellus lease was signed, and older Dunlevy-area deeds sometimes reserved coal separately from oil and gas, or bundled them together depending on the company and era. We trace that history through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds as part of confirming exactly what a family owns today.

sections.heading: What We Offer and Why
paragraphs: Once we've confirmed ownership and checked recent activity near your tract, we make a direct cash offer, no broker fee, no waiting on a listing. For a lot of Dunlevy-area families, especially those holding a smaller interest passed down through a mining or mill-working relative, that directness matters more than squeezing out the last possible dollar through a slower process.

faqs.question: Does my property being in the borough of Dunlevy itself affect my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It can, since in-town residential deeds sometimes carry a different mineral history than larger surrounding farmland. We check your specific recorded deed rather than assuming.

faqs.question: My family's deed mentions coal specifically. Do we still own oil and gas?
faqs.answer: It depends on how the original severance was worded. We trace the full chain of title through Washington County records to find out.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for selling my interest to you?
faqs.answer: No. We buy directly, so there's no broker commission or listing cost taken out of your offer.
